:::{#exm-convex-hull}
#### The convex hull of three points is a triangle

Let $S = \cb{\vzero, \vecf{e}_1, \vecf{e}_2} \subseteq \reals^2$, with $\vecf{e}_1 = \tp{(1, 0)}$ and $\vecf{e}_2 = \tp{(0, 1)}$,
and let $T = \cb{\vx \in \reals^2 : x_1 \ge 0,\ x_2 \ge 0,\ x_1 + x_2 \le 1}$, the filled triangle with corners $\vzero$, $\vecf{e}_1$ and $\vecf{e}_2$.
Then the [convex hull](#def-convex-hull) of $S$ is $T$: $\operatorname{conv}(S) = T$.

- $\operatorname{conv}(S) \subseteq T$.
  $T$ is the [intersection](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-indexed-intersection) of three [half-planes](#def-half-space),
  with $\vecf{a} = \tp{(1, 0)}$, $\tp{(0, 1)}$ and $\tp{(-1, -1)}$,
  and $c = 0$, $0$ and $-1$.
  Each half-plane $H = \cb{\vx : \dprod{\vecf{a}}{\vx} \ge c}$ is [convex](#def-convex-set):
  for $\vx, \vy \in H$ and $t \in [0, 1]$,

  $$
  \ba
  \dprod{\vecf{a}}{t \vx + (1 - t) \vy}
  &= t \dprod{\vecf{a}}{\vx} + (1 - t) \dprod{\vecf{a}}{\vy}
  && \text{(the dot product is linear)}
  \\
  &\ge t c + (1 - t) c
  && \text{(} \vx, \vy \in H \text{ and } t, 1 - t \ge 0 \text{)}
  \\
  &= c.
  && \text{(arithmetic)}
  \ea
  $$

  So $T$ is convex, by @thm-convex-intersection applied twice.
  $T$ contains $S$,
  so every point of $\operatorname{conv}(S)$ is in $T$.
- $T \subseteq \operatorname{conv}(S)$.
  Let $K$ be a [convex set](#def-convex-set) containing $S$,
  let $\vx \in T$,
  and let $s = x_1 + x_2$,
  so $0 \le s \le 1$.
  If $s = 0$, then $\vx = \vzero \in K$.
  Otherwise $\vecf{p} = \vx / s$ has $p_1 + p_2 = 1$ with $p_1, p_2 \ge 0$,
  so $\vecf{p} = p_1 \vecf{e}_1 + (1 - p_1) \vecf{e}_2$ is in $K$, by convexity with $t = p_1$.
  Then $\vx = s \vecf{p} + (1 - s) \vzero$ is in $K$, by convexity with $t = s$.
  So $\vx$ is in every convex set containing $S$.

@fig-convex-hull shows $S$, $T$ and the two steps for one point of $T$.
